summary: Returning the fixed required value takes constant work and matches the unavoidable constant lower bound, so runtime scaling has no genuine slower principal class.

optimality.argument: Every invocation must return one result and therefore requires Omega(1) work. The accepted function ignores all arguments and returns one fixed literal with O(1) work independent of argument count a.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required return value imposes a constant lower bound on every invocation.
The returned function performs one literal return and never reads, copies, or traverses its supplied arguments.
Cases cover zero and ten arguments, primitive values, null, objects, nested arrays, and strings resembling the required output.
